purpose: Goal-first technique definitions for editing a creator's own supplied footage. Entries are options, not quotas or automatic instructions.

evidence_scope_policy.transfer_rule: Evidence from swipe-feed short-form or advertising may inform a hypothesis, but cannot become a long-form default without a stated rationale and project-specific validation.
evidence_scope_policy.short_form_note: Fast cuts, persistent animated captions, aggressive vocal effects, and high intervention density may be valid scroll-stop conventions for TikTok, Reels, or Shorts profiles; this catalog does not treat them as universal YouTube long-form requirements.

evidence_levels.high: Direct repository proof, authoritative platform guidance, or convergent measured evidence for the stated narrow claim.
evidence_levels.moderate: Established craft practice or multiple practitioner sources with a plausible mechanism; outcome remains context-dependent.
evidence_levels.exploratory: Reference observation, practitioner hypothesis, or mechanism that needs project-specific testing.

capability_labels.proven_current: An existing repository path has focused functional evidence within its documented limits.
capability_labels.partial_current: Some ingredients exist, but the complete named technique or Studio control is not proven.
capability_labels.authoring_only: Codex can hand-author the result with Remotion or FFmpeg, but there is no versioned catalog-to-render path.
capability_labels.new_capability: No current supported implementation path was found.

techniques.name: Semantic tightening
avoid_when: the repetition escalates emotion or humor
the pause shows thought or authenticity

audiovisual_recipe.video: Remove only the redundant interval; cover a visible discontinuity with motivated B-roll or a clearly intentional reframing when useful.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Rebuild room tone and cadence; retain breaths or tails needed for natural phrasing.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: No quota. Tighten only passages where the shorter version preserves meaning and sounds intentional; sample dense sections at normal speed.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Do not clip phonemes, negations, names, or sentence boundaries. Keep captions and render-derived word timing aligned.

basis: YouTube recommends concise intros that immediately deliver promised value
repository rules R07-R10
working editors warn against line-by-line overcutting

success_evaluation: normal-speed listening for cadence and clipped words
independent render ASR and timing checks

capability.label: proven_current
capability.notes: Word-aware cut planning, pause handling, time maps, render verification, and reversible source preservation exist; authentic-footage editorial qualification remains pending.

techniques.name: Purposeful pause or uncut hold
avoid_when: dead air has no semantic or emotional function
the pause exposes an unwanted production mistake
a platform-specific short cannot afford the beat without losing the premise

audiovisual_recipe.video: Hold the face, action, or relevant visual instead of adding a change.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Preserve breath, room tone, or deliberate silence; optionally lower or stop music before the beat.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Derived from the performance and the contrast it creates. A pause is not good merely because it is long, and dense sections make rare pauses more potent.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Silence must not be mistaken for missing audio; captions may identify meaningful non-speech sound when needed.

basis: working editor Chris McCaleb describes silence as rhythm and meaning
pause experiments in educational video are mixed
repository rule R08

success_evaluation: normal-speed watch/listen for intention versus drag
owner judgment of emotional or comic timing
optional small comprehension test after dense explanations

capability.label: partial_current
capability.notes: The cut planner can preserve source pauses and bake can retain inserted silence, but Studio has no explicit pause proposal/control.

techniques.name: Motivated punch-in, pull-back, or alternate crop
avoid_when: source resolution cannot support the crop
the crop cuts hands or demonstration context

audiovisual_recipe.video: Change framing at a thought, emotion, or structural boundary; keep eyes and important gestures composed.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Usually unchanged; an accent is optional only if the beat calls for it.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Use only when a framing change carries meaning or solves continuity. Minimum gap and per-section density are profile preferences, not universal limits.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Protect lip visibility, signing, gestures, on-screen demonstrations, and caption-safe areas.

basis: practitioners motivate camera changes by punctuation, emotion, or thought boundaries
repository pixel tests prove bounded punch-in behavior

success_evaluation: verify the change corresponds to its stated beat

capability.label: proven_current
capability.notes: Versioned preserve-time punch-in exists in timeline extensions with pixel tests; Studio selection and semantic proposals are missing.

techniques.name: Evidence or demonstration cutaway
triggers: speaker references an object, document, screen, place, or result
a visible jump cut needs honest coverage
the claim benefits from primary visual evidence
avoid_when: visual contradicts or exaggerates the claim
the talking-head performance is the information

audiovisual_recipe.video: Show the relevant source at the moment it is discussed; preserve enough context to understand what is shown.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Usually retain creator narration; source audio is included only when it adds evidence and is mixed intelligibly.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Long enough to locate and understand the evidence; not extended merely to create visual churn.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Read important text aloud or integrate description; avoid unreadably brief or tiny screenshots.

basis: multimedia/signaling research supports relevant visuals and cues
practitioners distinguish illustrative B-roll from random B-roll
repository rules R17-R18

success_evaluation: audio-only comprehension check when the visual is essential

capability.label: proven_current
capability.notes: Cutaway, overlay, split, and insert types are implemented; semantic asset matching remains agent-authored.

techniques.name: J-cut or L-cut split edit
triggers: introduce the next scene before revealing it
carry narration across a visual change
smooth a dialogue or chapter transition
avoid_when: the source of a sound must be immediately visible

audiovisual_recipe.video: Offset the picture edit from the audio edit.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: J-cut: next audio leads; L-cut: previous audio continues over the next picture; add room-tone handles.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Use as continuity grammar, not an effect quota. The overlap must remain intelligible and semantically honest.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Captions should follow the heard speaker and not imply the person currently pictured is speaking when that is unclear.

basis: Adobe defines J-cuts as anticipation and L-cuts as continuity
standard documentary/interview practice

success_evaluation: no audible gap or clipped word

capability.label: partial_current
capability.notes: Cutaways already retain master narration, approximating an L-cut over B-roll. General independent split edits between arbitrary clips need a versioned model.

techniques.name: Dynamic highlight, pointer, or focus cue
triggers: visual search would distract from the explanation

audiovisual_recipe.video: Use one temporally aligned ring, arrow, crop, dimming mask, or cursor path around the relevant element.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Usually unchanged; a quiet UI cue may mark an actual interaction.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Start near the corresponding words and remove after the viewer can locate the target. Prefer one cue channel at a time.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Do not rely on color alone; preserve contrast and identify the target in speech or captions.

basis: 2026 cueing meta-analysis found context-dependent positive effects for visual/social cues and negative results for combined cue overload
dynamic signaling eye-tracking research

capability.label: authoring_only
capability.notes: Remotion examples contain rings, markers, highlights, and cursor motion, but there is no generic versioned timeline handler.

techniques.name: Selective key phrase, definition, or numeric text
avoid_when: verbatim text would duplicate every spoken word

audiovisual_recipe.video: Display the shortest text that resolves ambiguity or signals structure, placed near the relevant visual.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Keep speech primary; do not require an impact sound.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Readable for the phrase length and delivery size. Density follows information need, not a cadence timer.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Use sufficient contrast, size, dwell time, and captions. Verify spelling, names, numbers, and negations against audio.

basis: cueing research supports targeted text/color/highlight with moderation
WCAG requires synchronized captions for prerecorded meaningful audio

success_evaluation: small recall/comprehension test for key facts

capability.label: authoring_only
capability.notes: Many reusable TSX components and shots render text, but no generic proposal-to-render text technique exists.

techniques.name: Chapter reset or visual paragraph break
avoid_when: a card would interrupt emotional continuity
the label reveals a planned surprise

audiovisual_recipe.video: Use a clean cut, short title card, establishing visual, or consistent restrained transition.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Use room-tone continuity, a brief bridge, or an intentional music boundary.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: One per real structural boundary. Reuse consistent grammar so viewers learn what the transition means.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Speak or caption information that is essential; do not make the chapter card the only carrier of meaning.

basis: segmenting and coherence principles
practitioners describe restrained crossfades as paragraph breaks

capability.label: partial_current
capability.notes: Clean cuts, cutaways, inserts, crossfade, and custom cards exist; Studio has no semantic chapter palette.

techniques.name: Side-by-side comparison
avoid_when: comparison implies equivalence that is not supported

audiovisual_recipe.video: Place two clearly labeled sources in a stable layout with aligned time or explicit stills.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Choose one primary track or deliberately alternate; never allow competing speech.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Only as long as the viewer needs to compare the named property.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Use labels and narrated distinctions; verify each side at mobile viewing size.

basis: spatial/temporal contiguity principles
standard comparison practice

capability.label: proven_current
capability.notes: Split layout and crop validation exist with failure checks; semantic comparison UI is absent.

techniques.name: Cold open, proof-first preview, or unresolved promise
triggers: stakes can be shown without misrepresentation
avoid_when: clip promises material absent from the final edit

audiovisual_recipe.video: Open with a truthful outcome fragment, tension point, or concise premise, then establish the path to resolution.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Use original or narrated context sufficient to avoid a false implication.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: One opening structure, not repeated bait. Length is whatever delivers the premise clearly and quickly.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: The premise must be understandable with captions and must not depend solely on a rapid visual flash.

basis: YouTube says initial seconds should deliver the title/thumbnail promise and recommends testing intro styles
platform analytics can evaluate the first 30 seconds

success_evaluation: post-publication intro retention only when the owner supplies analytics

capability.label: authoring_only
capability.notes: A ColdOpenMontage example exists, but no general semantic cold-open model or Studio control exists.

techniques.name: Desaturation or tonal grade for a marked aside
avoid_when: the subject or product must be represented accurately
the device has become the default state
tone is solemn in a way the effect would trivialize

audiovisual_recipe.video: Apply a reversible bounded saturation/contrast treatment, optionally with a modest reframe.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Leave speech natural unless a separately justified timbre treatment is selected.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Bound to the marked thought. Frequency is learned per creator/video; the Atozy case study is evidence of a vocabulary, not a quota.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Do not use color removal as the only cue; preserve facial readability and contrast.

basis: direct Atozy case-study observation
repository color-grade pixel proof
no causal retention evidence

success_evaluation: post-publication analytics only as correlational feedback

capability.label: proven_current
capability.notes: Preserve-time saturation/contrast/brightness grade is implemented and pixel-tested; semantic selection and fades are not generic.

techniques.name: Brief vocal timbre or pitch treatment
avoid_when: the treatment could mock a protected characteristic or serious subject

audiovisual_recipe.video: Optionally pair with a restrained visual state change.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Apply a reversible, bounded pitch/formant/filter change with short crossfades and loudness matching; preserve the original track.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Use as punctuation, not default voice. Intensity and recurrence require owner preference and intelligibility proof.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Caption the exact words and meaningful non-speech character of the effect; compare processed and original audio under rule R12.

basis: practitioner use for comic emphasis
Atozy signal analysis showed inconsistent coincident spectral changes and does not establish one effect recipe

capability.label: new_capability
capability.notes: No versioned audio-effect handler exists. Installed Remotion is 4.0.486; official toneFrequency support for @remotion/media is documented from 4.0.520, and @remotion/media is not installed. Prefer a tested FFmpeg path or an explicitly reviewed upgrade.

techniques.name: Meaningful sound-effect punctuation
triggers: comic beat whose sound adds meaning
avoid_when: every cut already has an accent

audiovisual_recipe.video: Align to the visible or semantic event.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Use a short provenance-cleared effect, level below speech, with fades and no clipping.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Conditional on real beats. Silence between accents is part of the design.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Meaningful effects need caption equivalents; narration remains intelligible and mix QA is mandatory.

basis: practitioner consensus that well-timed sound can support humor/action
repository rule R23
overediting reports warn against effect-per-second mandates

capability.label: proven_current
capability.notes: Catalog mixing and procedural click/pop/tone are integrated; arbitrary generation is deferred.

techniques.name: Music arc and section-level energy shaping
triggers: connect a section without verbal clutter
avoid_when: complex explanation needs full verbal bandwidth

audiovisual_recipe.video: Let picture rhythm and music phrase support each other without forcing every cut to a beat.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Use licensed instrumental material, automation, ducking, and intentional entrances/exits.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Shape sections, not every sentence. Music may be absent for much of a video.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Speech remains primary; caption meaningful music changes where they carry narrative information.

basis: music-learning evidence is mixed and task-dependent
reviews find lyrics and difficult verbal tasks at greater risk
craft practice uses music for emotion and rhythm

capability.label: partial_current
capability.notes: Licensed catalog mixing, stems, and ducked SFX exist; a semantic music-arc model and general automation UI do not.

techniques.name: Music drop or contrastive silence
avoid_when: drop feels like an audio failure
speech edit clicks or room-tone discontinuity become exposed

audiovisual_recipe.video: Often hold or simplify picture at the drop.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Automate music down or out with a deliberate edge; preserve room tone and speech continuity.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Contrast only works when a prior state exists. Use at the strongest relevant beats, not mechanically.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Ensure the drop does not mask a word or suggest missing audio; caption meaningful silence only when needed for understanding.

basis: working-editor rhythm/silence practice
plausible contrast mechanism; no universal retention evidence

capability.label: authoring_only
capability.notes: Current mixing tools can implement level changes, but no catalog-to-automation path is proven.

techniques.name: Reaction hold and delayed cut
avoid_when: reaction is ambiguous or misleading out of context
hold exploits an unflattering accidental frame
consent/tone makes the close observation inappropriate

audiovisual_recipe.video: Stay on the reaction or cut to it after the line; resist immediate explanatory graphics.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Keep room tone, breath, laugh, or silence; optional music drop.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: The face and timing determine the hold. It should feel observed, not frozen by formula.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: If the reaction changes meaning, integrate it into description or narration for viewers who cannot see it.

basis: working editors stress reviewing all footage for non-verbal moments
performance-based craft practice

capability.label: partial_current
capability.notes: Current cut planning can retain handles and pauses, but reaction detection and explicit hold proposals are absent.

techniques.name: Freeze, replay, or slowed evidentiary moment
triggers: brief event is easy to miss
avoid_when: audio replay harms intelligibility or dignity

audiovisual_recipe.video: Replay once, freeze on the relevant frame, or slow a bounded action; label manipulation when confusion is possible.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Continue narration, mute/rebuild source audio, or replay only when editorially honest.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Only for moments whose meaning improves with added viewing time.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Explain the relevant event in speech/captions and identify altered speed or replay where needed.

basis: segmenting/temporal guidance principles
standard sports/tutorial/comedy practice

capability.label: new_capability
capability.notes: No generic freeze/replay/speed timeline extension was found.

techniques.name: Process compression via montage, omission, or speed-up
triggers: result matters more than every real-time action
avoid_when: compression makes a result look easier/faster than it was

audiovisual_recipe.video: Choose representative steps, use honest ellipsis, montage, or bounded speed-up, and show the resulting state.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Use narration, natural sound excerpts, or music; do not time-stretch critical speech casually.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Compress until each necessary causal step remains legible. No target shot length.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Captions and narration must still identify required steps; rapid montage must meet readability and flashing constraints.

basis: coherence/segmenting principles
acceleration meta-analysis warns that faster video can increase cognitive load and reduce learning outcomes

capability.label: partial_current
capability.notes: Omission and custom Remotion montages are possible; a generic speed-change extension is not implemented.

techniques.name: Setup, open loop, callback, and payoff
triggers: visual motif can return with new meaning
avoid_when: the payoff is absent or weak
too many unresolved threads burden memory

audiovisual_recipe.video: Plant a concise, truthful setup; preserve the relevant thread; return with recognizable but not identical visual/audio language.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Use repeated wording, sound motif, or a restrained bridge only when it helps recognition.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Limit simultaneous open loops to what the video can resolve cleanly. Do not use false mystery as filler.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: The setup and payoff must remain understandable through captions; visual-only callbacks need verbal or descriptive support when essential.

basis: YouTube recommends anticipation and thoughtful storytelling
narrative craft practice; no isolated causal retention estimate

success_evaluation: viewer can state what was resolved

capability.label: authoring_only
capability.notes: Codex can plan and author callbacks, but the project has no machine-readable narrative-thread model.

techniques.name: Match-on-action, eyeline, shape, or audio bridge
triggers: connect two ideas through analogous motion/shape/sound
avoid_when: match implies a factual connection that is not real
motion vectors or screen position cause disorientation

audiovisual_recipe.video: Align action phase, gaze, screen direction, geometry, or composition across the cut.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Carry a real or designed sound across the boundary when it supports the same continuity idea.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: A match is discovered from source relationships, not scheduled.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Continuity should not depend on subtle color alone; preserve spatial and narrative context.

basis: continuity-editing practice
event-segmentation research suggests cut-boundary attention depends on spatial alignment

capability.label: new_capability
capability.notes: No motion/eyeline/shape annotations or match proposal engine exists.

techniques.name: Nearly imperceptible slow push or drift
triggers: sustained statement that should not be cut
avoid_when: viewer should inspect a stable screen

audiovisual_recipe.video: Animate a few-percent crop change over a sustained passage with stable easing.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Unchanged.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Long and subtle enough not to read as a pulse. Use where holding the shot is preferable to cutting.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Provide a reduced-motion/no-drift profile option and keep critical content in frame.

basis: practitioner recommendation for sparing few-percent movement
no direct retention evidence

capability.label: authoring_only
capability.notes: Remotion interpolation can author this; the current FFmpeg punch-in is a bounded on/off effect rather than a slow animated move.

techniques.name: Deliberate non-use of effects
triggers: contrast will make a later intervention stronger
avoid_when: a visual is required to understand the claim
continuity error or unreadable evidence needs correction

audiovisual_recipe.video: Hold a well-composed source shot or use a clean cut only.
audiovisual_recipe.audio: Prioritize natural, intelligible speech and room tone; music/effects may be absent.

techniques.duration_intensity_frequency: Default candidate whenever an effect has no specific job. Restraint is not neglect; it still requires pacing, continuity, and technical QA.
techniques.accessibility_intelligibility: Essential captions, description, and readability remain required even in a restrained style.

basis: coherence and seductive-detail evidence
working editors report fatigue and story loss from constant stimulation
repository rules R15-R16

success_evaluation: ask whether any missing intervention blocks the intended goal
compare against effect-heavy alternative only when useful

capability.label: proven_current
capability.notes: The current pipeline can preserve source and use clean cuts; product work is needed to make no-effect an explicit proposal and accepted decision.
